authorities.title: Definition of contract
authorities.summary: Defines 'contract' as an agreement enforceable by law.

authorities.title: The Indian Contract Act, 1872
authorities.summary: States the conditions under which an agreement is enforceable as a contract.

authorities.title: The Indian Contract Act, 1872
authorities.summary: Deals with agreements to do acts impossible in themselves and with contracts becoming impossible or unlawful to perform.

authorities.title: The Indian Contract Act, 1872
authorities.summary: Provides for compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract.

authorities.title: Satyabrata Ghose v. Mugneeram Bangur & Co.
authorities.summary: Reported Indian Supreme Court decision often cited in relation to frustration/impossibility under Indian contract law. No verifiably confirmed official source URL identified in this review.

authorities.title: The Indian Contract Act, 1872
authorities.summary: Where a contract names a sum to be paid in case of breach, the party injured is entitled to reasonable compensation not exceeding the sum named, whether that sum was a genuine pre-estimate of loss or a penalty.
authorities._added_by: Person B, 2026-10-20 - the demo corpus raised late charges (Clause 8.1) and a not-a-penalty clause (Clause 8.3), and s.74 is the provision that governs both.

authorities.title: The Interest Act, 1978
authorities.summary: Where there is a written contract to pay interest at a rate, and no rate is named in the contract, the court may award interest at the rate the parties intended; where a rate is named, it runs from the due date.
authorities._added_by: Person B, 2026-10-20 - Clause 8.2 accrues interest at 12% per annum from the Payment Due Date.

authorities.title: The Specific Relief Act, 1963
authorities.summary: A contract that is not specifically enforceable is in general not enforced by a decree for specific performance but by damages; exclusion and limitation of liability clauses are among the arrangements a court will look through.
authorities._added_by: Person B, 2026-10-20 - the demo contract has termination for non-payment (Clause 12.3) and a liability cap (Clause 13.1).

authorities.title: The Information Technology Act, 2000
authorities.summary: Electronic records and electronic signatures are given the same legal recognition as paper records and handwritten signatures, so a contract executed by electronic means can satisfy a requirement that it be in writing and signed.
authorities._added_by: Person B, 2026-10-20 - Clause 7.2 requires electronic transfer and Clause 14.1 deems a notice served by email.

authorities.title: ONGC v. Great Eastern Shipping Co.
authorities.summary: The Supreme Court held that where a contract requires that modifications be in writing, an oral modification is not effective and the original terms continue to govern the parties.
authorities._added_by: Person B, 2026-10-20 - the case law behind the s.10 proviso, on the clause the engine flags as amendment_form.

authorities.title: Kailash Nath Associates v. Delhi Development Authority
authorities.summary: Damages are the normal remedy for breach and specific performance is an equitable remedy; a party that terminates a contract and then claims compensation must prove the loss it says it has suffered.
authorities._added_by: Person B, 2026-10-20 - the demo contract caps aggregate liability and lets the Supplier terminate for non-payment.

authorities.title: State of Karnataka v. Shree Guru Dutt Sharma
authorities.summary: Delay in performance is not automatically fatal: a party is entitled to a reasonable extension of time where the delay is not culpable, and forfeiture of earnest money requires proof of default and of the loss caused.
authorities._added_by: Person B, 2026-10-20 - the demo contract has a 15-day cure period running from receipt of written notice.

authorities.title: Motilal Padampat Sugar Mills Co. v. State of Uttar Pradesh
authorities.summary: Frustration of a contract by impossibility or illegality discharges the parties; the court will not remake the bargain for them, and a party claiming frustration must show the impossibility was not self-created.
authorities._added_by: Person B, 2026-10-20 - the demo contract has a force majeure clause (Clause 15.1), which s.56 and the older authorities did not reach on the clause's own wording.
